cards.name: Default Settings
cards.id: Custom Data/Preflight Styles/Default Settings.pfs#Default Settings
cards.summary: Preflight style file (.pfs) shipped with CorelDRAW 2024: a saved set of document checks, not something with a look. No thumbnail exists (the sheet marks it 'not visual'); the file is plain text and was read: 81 check entries, each switched Enabled=1 or Enabled=0, grouped by target. PDF export has 11 checks (6 on, 5 off), printing has 32 (26 on, 6 off), and HTML export (12), SVG export (12) and SWF export (14) are all on. The checks that are off are the bitmap and vector colour-mode warnings (BitmapCMYK, BitmapRGB, VectorCMYK, VectorRGB, for both PDF and print), the TrueType-font warning (UsedTT, for both) and, for print, the small-font-size warning (FontSizeBelow); the rest are on, including low image resolution, missing links, small fonts, hidden or non-printable layers, spot-colour conversion and overprint.
use_for: a sensible starting point for checking a document before print or PDF export
keeping one shared set of checks across a team
a base to copy and tighten for a printer's rules
avoid: Strict print jobs: the colour-mode warnings are off here, so RGB or CMYK mix-ups will not be flagged; switch them on or load a printer's own style.
Expecting it to fix problems: it only reports them.
Assuming the control name in the app: the harvest did not find the exact dialog, so check the Preflight tab of the Print and Publish to PDF dialogs.
cards.applies_to: the open document's preflight run, not an object: the style sets which checks run when the document is checked before print, PDF, HTML, SVG or SWF output
cards.how_to_apply: In the Preflight settings (Preflight tab of the Print dialog or Publish to PDF), choose or load the style named 'Default Settings'; the exact control name was not confirmed by the harvest. File: <CorelDRAW 2024 install folder>/Custom Data/Preflight Styles/Default Settings.pfs (plain text, read). Script: no call that loads a preflight style was found.

verified.note: Not visual; the .pfs INI was parsed in review: 81 sections, PDF 11 (6 on, 5 off), print 32 (26 on, 6 off), HTML 12, SVG 12 and SWF 14 all on, and the switched-off checks are exactly the ones the card lists.

cards.name: tilt

The sheet shows 'render failed' (no thumbnail), so the file was decoded instead: the last 4096 bytes are exactly 1024 little-endian 32-bit values, and in tilt they rise in a straight line, two samples per step, from 264 to 781 on what looks like a 0-1023 scale (about 26 percent to 76 percent). A straight, sloping curve like this should slant the picture in one direction instead of bending it. The effect of the file on a picture was not rendered, so the direction is unverified.

a simple lean for a bitmap logo
